title: ||:GIRLS:||:CHANCE:||:MUSIC:|| by Eisa Davis at Vineyard Theatre #gir...
transcript: This was kind of like Stereophonic but with mentally ill teenagers. Eisa Davis has written an aching ode to the impermanence of relationships despite their lasting effects. Ephemerality is the whole point — the experiences these characters have are just as fleeting as the notes they play throughout the summer music program we see them going through. It's a slow burn, and while the plot could use a bit more focus here and there, I kind of enjoyed the scattered nature of it. To me, it evokes pointillism. We're meant to take in the individual and disparate slices of characterization in order to see the bigger picture. What is consistent is the comedically blunt yet endearing delivery of the script and the incredible musicianship among the actors. I would have loved for the play to incorporate even more music, but I understand that as a character study, it's probably more interesting to see them grapple with things they're uncertain about, and music is not one of them. With that, another program for my collection.
